articleTitle: Reliability-Based Design of a 5 MWp Centralized Solar Photovoltaic Power Plant with Multi-String Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Centralized photovoltaic solar energy plants are systems for converting solar energy into electricity, concentrating this generation process in a single location. This type of plant presents specific characteristics and technical and regulatory challenges to be implemented. Concepts such as Reliability, and Multi-String Arrangement are applied to ensure system reliability. Furthermore, sizing methods are employed, using detailed hourly solar irradiation data for a specific region. The Capacity Outage Probability Table (COPT), Expected Supplied Energy (ESE), and Capacity Factor are calculated for each case study. The overall objective is to improve understanding and efficiency in developing centralized photovoltaic plants.

articleTitle: Input filter capacitance design method for DC-DC converters in PV systems applications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a new design method for filter capacitors connected between photovoltaic panels and DC-DC converters operating in continuous or discontinuous conduction mode. The method considers the energy transferred through voltage ripple in the panel and its electrical circuit model. The approach allows for the determination of energy transfer efficiency and defines the required voltage ripple and filter capacitance. The capacitance and input voltage ripple for a DCDC Boost converter are evaluated, defining the average values needed for efficiencies in transferring photovoltaic panel energy of $\mathbf{9 8 \%}, \mathbf{9 9 \%}$, and $\mathbf{9 9. 9 \%}$. A Boost converter operating with a photovoltaic array of 760 W, a switching frequency of 30 kHz, a peak-to-peak current ripple at the input of $100 \%$, and an output voltage of 380 V was implemented to validate the models.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of a Dual Active Bridge Converter with a Variable Inductor for Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the integration of a variable inductor into a dual-active-bridge (DAB) converter for battery charging applications, emphasizing efficiency improvements. The variable inductor introduces an additional degree of freedom to conventional single-phase-shift modulation. By adjusting the inductance, the converter achieves optimal soft switching and minimizes current circulation, surpassing the performance of the traditional phase-shift method with a fixed inductor, specially under extreme output power conditions. To validate this approach, a 600 W prototype converter was developed to charge a lead-acid battery-bank. The efficiency of the DAB with the variable inductor was measured and compared to that of the DAB with fixed inductor across the full range of the battery voltage and power. Experimental results demonstrate that the DAB converter with variable inductor achieves superior performance for battery charging compared to the traditional DAB with fixed inductor under both low and high-load conditions.

articleTitle: Model reference adaptive voltage control of photovoltaic boost converter
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article aims to present a methodology for adaptive control of a boost converter through two loops based on a Model Reference. This methodology makes it possible to reduce the input capacitance of the boost converter, increasing the response speed and consequently the efficiency of tracking the maximum power point. In the introduction section, the problem involving the reduction of input capacitance in boost converters is presented. In the next sections, mathematical modeling of the converter is carried out, and a model for voltage transfer function related to inductor’s current was obtained, and finaly a model for current transfer funcion related to duty-cycle. The last section presents simulation results, demonstrating the stability of controller under several parametrics variations. Finnaly, a comparison among an adaptive controller and a classical controller was presented.

articleTitle: Enhancing Aircraft Control: Design and Implementation of an Electromechanical Actuator control System with State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper aims to guarantee the safety, stability and efficiency of aircraft through the precise control of ailerons, depth gauges and rudders, using cutting-edge technologies such as power-by-wire actuation. The implementation involves detailed mathematical modeling of the system, closed-loop simulations, and the consideration of non-linear effects and disturbances, ensuring robust and reliable performance in various flight conditions.

articleTitle: Cascaded Adaptive Predictive Controller: An Essential Approach to Face the New Challenges in Sustainable Energy System Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive predictive controller with two cascaded loops, combining the benefits of cascade control techniques with the robustness and stability of gradient-type algorithms. The controller is designed to mimic cascaded linear controllers while providing adaptability to varying plant dynamics. By utilizing a gradient-type algorithm, it determines crucial parameters for effective plant control, enhancing its tracking capabilities and stability. To showcase the proposed controller’s advantages and limitations, an extensive mathematical simulation is conducted. These simulations demonstrate its ability to precisely track references and swiftly adapt to abrupt variations in the reference signal. The results highlight the controller’s optimal tracking performance and remarkable adaptability, underscoring its potential for real-world applications in dynamic systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control Applied to Half-Bridge Synchronous Buck Converter using LCL Filter for Charging Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes a discrete-time Model Reference Adaptive Controller (MRAC), applied to a Half-Bridge synchronous buck converter for charging batteries. The system uses an LCL filter that interfaces the power converter and the batteries. A virtual plant method is proposed for better transitory response of the adaptive control system. The model reference utilizes a reduced order, to simplify the project of the adaptive controller. Simulation results are presented for validation of the control project.

articleTitle: Study of Bidirectional DC-DC Converters Based on the Buck-Boost Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents different topologies of bidirectional DC-DC converters based on the buck-boost topology. Four topologies are discussed: bidirectional buck-boost, switched inductor cell, switched inductor and capacitor cell, and $R^{2} P^{2}$. Theoretical analysis and simulations are performed for each topology, aiming to evaluate their performance in terms of voltage gain and voltage stresses on semiconductors. The results show that the topologies exhibit high voltage gains and voltage stresses similar to those of the buck-boost topology. Moreover, the $\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathbf{2}} \boldsymbol{P}^{\mathbf{2}}$ topology demonstrated the highest static gain and lower current stresses. All topologies exhibited good performance in terms of bidirectionality.

articleTitle: Biweight Midcorrelation and Dynamic Time Warping-Based Pilot Protection Applied to a Line Connecting a DFIG-Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the application of two novel pilot protection algorithms on a transmission line that connects a DFIG-based wind turbine to a power grid. The first algorithm is based on the Biweight Midcorrelation (BWMC) between the currents of the protected line terminals, while the second relies on the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) between these currents. In previous research on these methods, cases covering lines that integrate wind power generation, which are increasingly more present in the context of smart and sustainable energy systems, were not considered. Therefore, this article shows that both algorithms constitute viable and effective options also to protect lines connecting wind power generation, extending the research results concerning these two new line pilot protection solutions. The algorithms were tested in cases involving faults at different points along the line and with different fault resistances, and the results show that, by also using the zero-sequence currents alongside the phase currents, both methods can detect diverse kinds of internal faults, even those with $1000 \Omega$ resistance.

articleTitle: Challenges of inverter-based load disaggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This document addresses the challenges of disaggregating techniques for non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) of inverter-based loads. Although inverter-based loads are more energy efficient they add an extra layer of complexity for NILM-based algorithms because of their variable energy consumption and rapid variations. There are few studies regarding these types of loads and they do not cover every combination of loads such as several inverter-based loads in the same energy network. There are several questions on whether or not such algorithms can be used for real-time applications because of their apparent high computational need and their storage requirements to perform the disaggregation.

articleTitle: Finite Elements Analysis Applied to the Design of Integrated Magnetics for Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Accurate modeling of inductors is critical to optimize their performance, volume, and efficiency, especially in high-frequency and high-power applications. Traditional two-stage LED drivers currently have two separate magnetics, one for each converter inductor. However, these standalone magnetics are bulky and take up a significant volume within the driver. Nevertheless, these inductors can be integrated into a single core, aiming to reduce the volume and, consequently, the system’s overall power density. This article presents a detailed comparison of finite elements of two standalone magnetics and one integrated magnetic, using the same electrical and magnetic design specifications in an LED driver application, applying the finite elements analysis in Ansys Electronics® software. The inductors are designed for a 180W LED driver using an integrated converters configuration, in which a Boost converter is the power factor correction stage and the Buck converter is the power control stage, both operating in DCM. The simulation results show that a volume reduction of 20% is obtained when implementing the integrated magnetic instead of the standalone magnetics for the given design specifications.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Interconnected Power Systems using the Lyapunov Criterion.
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the stability analysis of an interconnected power system made up of a photovoltaic solar panel and a DC-DC converter. Stability is demonstrated through the use of the Lyapunov criterion for two types of systems. The first consists of the panel interconnected to a Boost converter and the second uses a Buck converter. The dynamic equation of the panel’s behavior is obtained through the connection of a capacitor to its output. The resulting system is analyzed by means of a candidate Lyapunov function to demonstrate stability in some sense. The dynamic behavior of the considered states in the face of variations in the control input is graphed to visualize their convergence to an equilibrium point. The methodology presented through the development of the paper can be extended to systems that include higher order converters.

articleTitle: Bio-inspired linear quadratic tracker for DC motors speed control
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: The wind is intermittent. This fact makes it necessary to equip the wind turbines with actuators to adjust the yaw and pitch angles of the wind turbine to maximize power generation. Commonly, DC motors are used as actuators in this kind of system. This paper presents a methodology for optimizing a linear quadratic regulator used to control the actuator of a wind turbine. The procedure is based on the sand cat swarm algorithm along with a set of systematic rules to ensure that the optimized controller minimizes the tracking error and respects the system constraints. The results show the feasibility of the developed method for controller tuning and satisfactory performance of the system, where the transient regimes end in less than 0.005 s without overshoots.

articleTitle: Steady-State and Dynamic Tests of Overcurrent Protection through Real-Time Digital Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: There are many reasons to test a protection relay. To perform a relay test, conventionally a test-set equipment is used. However, today’s relays are highly sophisticated with several settings, protocols, and a high number of inputs and outputs. Real-time simulators (RTS) are often applied for hardware-in-the-loop studies in complex cases. This paper will explore some possibilities of relay testing using the Typhoon HIL RTS. Still, this paper shows that RTS can be used not only for complex dynamic system relay tests, but also for other types of tests, such as steady-state and dynamic tests. All the testing results are performed with HighPROTEC MRA4 relay and compared with the Conprove CE-6006 test-set.

articleTitle: An Eight-Switch Nine-Level Common-Ground Inverter with Four-fold Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Transformerless inverters with common-ground concept have been gaining interest due to their advantages especially for grid-tied photovoltaic systems. The zero-commom mode voltage mitigates the leakage current enhancing the safety reducing the electromagnetic interference. This paper proposes a nine-level common-ground transformerless inverter with only eight switches, three diodes and four capacitors. In addition, the inverter presents an inherent quadruple gain dismissing additional conversion stages in a generation system. The paper outlines the various modes of operation, the design guidelines and a control strategy the closed-loop operation of the inverter. Finally, the performance of the proposed inverter is verified through simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Switched Control Design for a Modified SEPIC Converter Applied to PEF Generation.
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper describes the modification of a DCDC converter and the controller design that allows generating a PEF (Pulsed Electric Field) for food treatment purposes. Recent literature focused on food processing mentions that the application of short-duration voltage pulses helps to better preserve food because it prevents the microorganisms proliferation. Derived from the condition of generating high voltage pulses at a high frequency, a state-time dependent switching control law is designed. The simulation results of the modified converter imply that its implementation in a real application environment is feasible. The impedance used to apply the PEF considers the electrical characteristic conductivity of a liquid medium such as milk, which can have a value between 4.0 and 5.0 mS at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: Cost and Efficiency Optimization of Low-frequency Transformers in Uninterruptible Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach for optimizing both cost and efficiency in low-frequency transformers used in ferro-resonant UPS systems. Detailed loss models for the core and windings are provided, along with experimental measurements to ensure accuracy. A cost table for magnetic materials, such as copper, aluminum, and different silicon steel grades, is used as a reference for evaluating their impact on transformer performance and expense. Using Pareto fronts, the study performs a multi-objective optimization of transformer designs for 700 VA and 1.5 kVA UPS systems. The results demonstrate that significant cost reductions can be achieved while enhancing efficiency by employing advanced optimization techniques. For the 1.5 kVA transformer, the study shows that modifications can substantially lower costs without compromising performance. However, the 700 VA transformer design is already optimal and lying on the Pareto front, where further cost reduction would reduce efficiency.

articleTitle: Volume Reduction of an Integrated Magnetic in a Two-Stage Street-Lighting LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes the volume reduction of an integrated magnetic in a two-stage LED driver, aiming to increase the system’s overall power density. The enhancement of the integrated magnetic design is detailed and compared with two standalone magnetics in the same LED driver configuration and using identical electrical and magnetic design specifications. This work’s main contribution and objective is the utilization of a different version of the integrated magnetic to decrease the total volume of the LED driver over the previous integrated magnetic design. To verify the feasibility of this change, the paper analyzes the theoretical equivalent magnetic circuits and simulation results using Finite Element Method (FEM) through Ansys Electronics® software, as well as PSIM software for core loss calculations, and efficiency was measured using the Yokogawa WT1800 power analyzer. The proposed design was validated by the implementation of a 180W two-stage street-lighting LED driver, which employs a Boost converter in critical conduction mode as the power factor correction (PFC) stage and a Buck converter in continuous conduction mode as the power control (PC) stage. Implementing the new integrated magnetic enabled a volume reduction of 40% compared to its earlier version. Furthermore, an additional advantage of this work was the LED driver global efficiency increase of at least 0.15% throughout the entire LED dimming range, between 10 and 100% of the load nominal operation, in comparison to the prototype with the prior integrated magnetic. When the efficiency enhancement is compared with the commercial LED driver, there is an efficiency improvement of over 1.2% through the same LED dimming interval, without any electrical modifications in the LED driver itself.

articleTitle: Implementation of an FPGA Driven Single-phase Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a single-phase H-bridge multilevel inverter with the option of a three- or five-level output, which is driven by an FPGA. This inverter is suitable for teaching and research activities about multilevel inverters in power electronics. The selection of the number of levels of the inverter is done with selector switches on the FPGA board. The topology used to generate three and five levels was of the Symmetrical Cascade Inverter type. For the development of the inverter, a sinusoidal PWM modulation technique with carriers in phase was used, in which the frequency was 2.5 kHz for the carriers and 60 Hz for the modulator. The circuit is controlled by a programmable logic device FPGA through VHDL language. Simulations were performed using the software PSIM to analyze the waveforms of each inverter. Finally, the results of the inverter output on a resistive load using an oscilloscope are presented.

articleTitle: Financial Viability of PV Grid for an Intelligent System of Residential Buildings in sub-urban Areas of Punjab, Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: With fuel prices rising and environmental concerns intensifying, the financial burden on consumers and businesses has shown an upward trajectory, prompting a search for sustainable alternatives sources. This study investigates the financial feasibility of installing a grid-tied solar photovoltaic (PV) system in residential buildings in suburban areas of Punjab, Pakistan. The research uses a complete intelligent financial model to assess the feasibility of a grid-connected solar PV system, incorporating parameters such as solar irradiance levels, system size, capital costs, operating expenses, energy rates, its incentives, and payback periods in a systematic computational optimization methodology. The shift to solar photovoltaic systems provides an affordable way to lower energy bills that can also lessen the dependency on fossil fuels. Additionally, solar PV systems help significantly to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and environmental damages by utilizing the clean energy of the sun. This is in line with worldwide efforts to battle climate change and protect the planet from environmental concerns. This research uses RET Screen software to evaluate the financial feasibility with GHG reduction analysis as well. The study’s findings are useful for homeowners, policymakers, and stakeholders interested in encouraging renewable energy adoption and sustainable development in Punjab, Pakistan’s suburban region.

articleTitle: Microinverter Topology using Isolated Interleaved Boost with 3-Level T-Type Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Microinverter technology has become promising in recent years, with positive impacts on the production of photovoltaic (PV) solar energy. Therefore, there is a growing need to develop and evaluate new microinverter topologies. Thus, this article proposes a microinverter topology based on the combination of an isolated interleaved boost converter with a 3-level T-type inverter. The proposed topology, as well as its mathematical modeling are introduced in the research. Furthermore, the control system used in this work uses a PSO MPPT algorithm to track the maximum power point and a cascade control with PLL for synchronization with electrical grid. Simulation results, using PSIM software, are presented in order to show the effectiveness of this proposal. In this case, tests are performed, in which changes in irradiation in PV panel are carried out, thus demonstrating the correct functioning of control system used.

articleTitle: PCB Layout Design Using Finite Element Analysis for Parasitic Inductance Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology employing Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation to evaluate parasitic elements in two distinct PCB layouts of 1000 W full-bridge power inverters designed with SMD-based components. The study compares a two-layer PCB (Layout 1) with a four-layer PCB (Layout 2), where the latter features a reduced spacing of 0.196 mm between conductive planes. The results show that the reduced spacing in Layout 2 leads to an increase in capacitance and a significant reduction of approximately 59.46% in AC inductance. This methodology is adaptable for different power converters and PCB layouts, enabling designers to optimize mechanical dimensions, component arrangements, and configurations before prototyping.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shielding Losses Between Transformer Windings Considering Harmonic Components
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: As the demand for energy increases and the need for more robust transformers to withstand harmonic voltage and current distortions continues to grow, the use of electrostatic shielding becomes crucial to mitigate harmonic-induced losses. Using computer simulations based on the finite element method with ANSYS Maxwell® software, this study analyzes the frequency response of losses in low-voltage windings and shields. The shield analysis reveals a quadratic pattern as the rated current percentage increases, but unlike LV windings, the behavior is similar for all frequencies. The concentration of losses occurs at the ends of the windings and shields, intensified by the increase in frequency due to the pericular effect. It can be concluded that a thermal analysis is needed to assess the impact of losses in the shields on the transformer’s temperature, since heat spots can accelerate the ageing of the insulation and generate harmful gases.

articleTitle: Modelling of an Induction Motor and Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) for Speed Estimation in Xcos
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Techniques based on Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) are considered as effective approaches for speed estimation due to their commendable performance and direct stability analysis. Different works about the application of MRAS in speed sensorless control of induction motor can be found in literature. However, students usually have problems to understand and implement MRAS algorithm. On the other hand, open source softwares allow students to understand and simulate algorithm, as students can be easily watch, analyze and edit the block diagram. Hence, this paper introduces the block diagram of a 3-phase induction motor and the MRAS algorithm developed in SCILAB/Xcos. SCILAB is an open-source software that include a block diagram simulation interface called Xcos. The MRAS algorithm in this work compares the rotor flux estimated by a reference model and an adjustable model (that depends on the mechanical speed), to get a flux estimation error. A PI regulator adjust the mechanical speed value in the adjustable model to reduce that error. The block diagrams of the dq0 induction model and the MRAS algorithm developed in Xcos and presented in this work allow student to easily understand both algorithms, widely used in motor drives. It is worth to mention that authors did not find any MRAS diagram implemented in Xcos in literature.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Leakage Inductance in Multi-Winding Coupled Inductors for Flyback-Based LED Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on the estimation of leakage inductance in multi-winding coupled inductors used in flyback converters for LED lighting applications. Leakage inductance is a critical factor that affects the efficiency and reliability of flyback converters, leading to increased power consumption, electromagnetic interference, and potential damage to the converter. The study explores the use of Finite Element Analysis (FEA) 3D modeling to analyze. Two simplification models, Standard and Dowell’s Simplification, are implemented and compared. The results obtained from FEA simulations are validated against experimental measurements taken with an LCR meter. The findings indicate that both simplification models offer a good balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, with Dowell’s model better performance in reducing the error margin.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive control for BLDC motor control: synthesis and experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are increasingly favored in various applications due to their high efficiency and reliability. However, maintaining satisfactory performance under varying operating conditions and system uncertainties remains a challenge. This paper presents a robust model reference adaptive control to improve the performance of BLDC motors. The main advantage of this control approach in relation to well-established fixed-gain controllers is its robustness features to better handle parameter variations and external disturbances. In this sense, this work presents an adaptive control structure, which merges the classical MIT rule-based adaptive control structure with a majorant signal and $\sigma$-function to ensure robustness to the resulting controller. This controller dynamically adjusts controller gains to provide consistent and responsive motor performance. Experimental results corroborate the effectiveness of the developed controller.

articleTitle: Control of DC-DC converters in DC microgrids: adaptation of virtual DC machine control
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Technological advances in the field of power electronics have made direct current (DC) more viable, paving the way for the so-called DC microgrids. In microgrids, it is quite common to provide the power electronic converters with some kind of droop control to properly and automatically share the required load. With DC-DC converters, the simplest way to do that is using the concept of virtual resistance, but it does not provide any inertial response necessary to improve the voltage quality and guarantee the microgrid’s stability. Alternatively, there is the concept of a virtual DC machine, which allows the load share and the desired inertial response. In this context, this paper adapts this idea in such a way that the control loops are cascaded and the similarities with the DC machine are clearer. The innermost loop controls the converter’s output voltage, considering two possibilities for this part: one open-loop-based and another closed-loop-based. The cascaded outer loops implement the electromagnetic and electromechanical dynamics of the DC machine and the effect of the governor. A detailed methodology is provided for setting the machine parameters according to the desired dynamics. Simulations are carried out to compare the proposed virtual DC machine with a regular virtual-resistance-based droop approach. The results show smother dynamics for the proposed control, while maintaining the proper load share.

articleTitle: Adaptive Proportional-Resonant Current Control applied to Grid-Connected Converters using L Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive proportional-resonant control strategy for three-phase inverters connected to the electrical grid using an L filter. The control strategy aims to enhance harmonic compensation and improve the quality of current injected into the grid by utilizing a damped resonant controller with adaptive controller based on model reference. The adaptive control adapts to the fundamental frequency, while the proportional resonant control attenuates up to the 11th harmonic. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy, demonstrating its capability to dynamically adjust control parameters and maintain system stability under varying conditions.

articleTitle: Control of a Satellite Antenna Using Servomechanism Controller and State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design and control of a satellite antenna system using a servomechanism controller and state observer to achieve precise positioning despite noise, actuator saturation, and parametric variations. The integration of a state observer enhances velocity estimation accuracy, improving control performance. Simulation results demonstrate robust performance across various scenarios, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in managing noise, disturbances, and actuator limitations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Solid-State Transformer Features Through Modeling and Control Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The adoption of efficient and sustainable technologies in the electric power sector is essential due to the increasing demand and the need to integrate distributed energy resources. In this context, conventional transformers have significant limitations, while the Solid-State Transformer (SST) offers better control of power quality and integration with renewable sources. The SST has the potential to transform the electric power sector, but additional research is needed on its control, high-power operation, and economic feasibility. This work aims to model and control a three-stage SST operating at low power with equal input and output voltage levels using Matlab Simulink software. The results show improvements in power quality, such as voltage regulation, THD reduction, and power factor correction, in addition to facilitating more efficient integration of renewable sources, underscoring the SST’s potential over conventional transformers.

articleTitle: Design of a Wireless Charging Hub for Smart and IoT Devices Using Magnetic Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This project uses simulations to illustrate the present status of contemporary wireless charging. Wireless charging has changed the environment in today’s society. Wireless charging has decreased worldwide plastic use while also improving environmental advantages. When it comes to charging devices, the wireless charging system surpasses the cable charging method. This project demonstrates how to utilize wireless charging to simultaneously power several smart devices. The project’s original work included wireless charging for a large number of devices at once, including Alexa, smartwatches, smartphones, laptops, and Arduino. The technology in this project is designed to allow for varying distances between the transmitter and receiver. Users will have more control over how they use and charge their devices as a result of this. As a result, if Arduino and sensors used in IoT applications can be fueled wirelessly, it would open the way for IoT breakthroughs.

articleTitle: Implementation of a research assistant for literature review with Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The scientific literature presents a significant challenge for researchers seeking to stay abreast of their fields. Traditional keyword-based search methods often prove inadequate, leading to information overload and missed connections. This paper introduces RAAI (Research Assistant based on Artificial Intelligence), a novel tool that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to revolutionize literature exploration for Systematic Literature Review (SLR). RAAI utilizes the power of LLMs to understand individual research contexts and retrieve highly relevant articles, facilitating a deeper and more personalized systematic literature review. Developed using Python and the Streamlit library, RAAI offers an intuitive web interface for managing keywords, mining databases (IEEE Xplore, arXiv, Elsevier Scopus), and filtering articles with an AI-powered relevance assessment. This allows researchers to target relevant publications and manage the reviewing process efficiently.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Visible Light Communication Link
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) uses light intensity modulation to transmit data while simultaneously maintaining the primary function of LEDs illuminating the environment. This study focuses on the implementation and analysis of experimental results from a unidirectional VLC communication link. It presents a detailed analysis of each component of a generic VLC system, examining their functions and exploring possible topologies and methodologies for their implementation. Following this, the constituent blocks of the developed VLC system are analyzed using the same methodology, but with a focus on the specific topologies employed. Finally, the results of the experimental tests conducted with the system developed in this study are discussed. In summary, this work focuses on the implementation of an end-to-end VLC link using well-established topologies and techniques from the literature.

articleTitle: Lifetime Analysis of MOSFETs in UPS Application Through Experimental Thermal Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: One of the main difficulties in UPS design and lifetime estimation is determining how it will be used, since load-level and duration of battery-mode are strongly dependent on the user profile. Thus, it is necessary to investigate how the load and battery cycle duration affect the thermal behavior of the power semiconductors. This paper presents an experimental electro-thermal characterization of MOSFETs in a low-power Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) and models their operating temperature in battery mode across different load levels and types. The study examines both linear and non-linear loads, with battery mode duration ranging from 1 to 60 minutes. The results indicate that the UPS used as a case study is incapable of sustaining extended battery mode operations for loads exceeding 800 W or VA. Additionally, non-linear loads significantly accelerate the degradation of the MOSFETs’ lifespan.

articleTitle: Analysis of Input Current Ripple in Interleaved Boost Converters with PWM Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This study explores PWM modulation strategies for interleaved N-cell Boost converters, emphasizing phase angle variation between carriers and operational points, analyzing both Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) and Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM). The research shows that equidistant phase shifts minimize input current ripple. Points for ripple reduction and cancellation are identified, demonstrating effectiveness in both modes. The results indicate that optimizing the number of cells and the modulation strategy can significantly reduce current ripple, enhancing the efficiency of renewable energy sources like photovoltaic panels and fuel cells. This approach also reduces the size, cost, and complexity of additional filtering components, offering a robust solution for improving energy conversion systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of angular velocity estimation methods for reaction wheel inverted pendulum control
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The reaction wheel inverted pendulum (RWIP) is widely used in education and research due to its complex and unstable dynamics, representing a classic challenge in control engineering. Although various controllers such as PID, LQR, and swing-up techniques are applied to stabilize the RWIP, the presence of measurement noise can compromise the accuracy of the angular velocity estimation of the pendulum. This study aims to develop and compare the effectiveness of a reduced-order state estimator versus a differentiator in stabilizing the RWIP using state feedback with pole placement. The methodology involves the mechanical and electrical modeling of the system, followed by the design of a state feedback controller. Simulations were conducted in MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the performance of the two angular velocity estimation methods in the presence of measurement noise. The inclusion of realistic elements such as actuator saturation and system nonlinearities ensures the practical applicability of the controller.

articleTitle: Minimizing Losses and Optimizing Energy Flow in Power Distribution Systems Using the Transportation Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this paper, the transport problem is applied to optimize the power flow of an energy distribution system. Two case studies are analyzed, covering different scenarios with variations in generation values, load and cost of energy loss. The main objective of this study is to improve the efficiency of energy transport, aiming to identify the optimal paths to meet energy demand. The transport method is implemented through the Otimiza software, where the case study code is developed. Through this approach, the optimization method allows for the efficient allocation of energy resources, minimizing operational costs and maximizing demand satisfaction. The results of this study reveal the ability of the transportation method to improve power flow management in distribution systems, providing a better balance between generation and demand.

articleTitle: Rotor Speed Observer Based on Extended Stator Current Model of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a sensorless control for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs). The rotor speed estimation is based on linearized dynamic model of stator currents in the synchronous reference frame. This extended model becomes simpler for creating the estimator, since it does not vary sinusoidally like the model in the stationary reference frame. The estimated rotor angular position can be obtained from the rotor speed estimation. The Lyapunov stability analysis for systems in the discrete time domain is used to find an adaptation law for the rotor speed estimation, so that the sensorless control system is stable. Simulation and HIL results are presented to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Voltage Control Strategy for UPS: MRAC and Resonant Control Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes a discrete-time model reference adaptive controller (MRAC) via a state-feedback approach, combined with multiple resonant controllers for sinusoidal tracking. The application of this hybrid controller is for voltage control in the output stage of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) under nonlinear load variations. In this design, the MRAC is dedicated to tracking the fundamental frequency, while the resonant controllers manage the rejection of sinusoidal disturbances, resulting in a significantly lower computational burden. The proposed hybrid controller demonstrates satisfactory performance in both reference signal tracking and disturbance rejection. Simulation results, considering nonlinear load variations, confirm the effective regulation of the output voltage, low total harmonic distortion (THD), successful disturbance rejection, and accurate error tracking in steady-state.

articleTitle: Use of Dynamic Simulation for Control Analysis of DC-DC Converters - A Case Study using Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The exercise of performing dynamic simulations that characterize physical devices allows the validation of theoretical analytical models in a practical way. A clear understanding of the dynamic operation of the different DC-DC converter topologies allows the development of appropriate automatic control strategies. This work presents the use of dynamic simulation environments to study the behavior of the buck-boost converter related to the application of different pulse width modulation (PWM) input values. The main contribution of this work is the methodological description of the simulation environmental construction process, as well as the construction of a knowledge base that allows efficient automatic control actions for this type of converter.

articleTitle: Development of Bidirectional Hybrid DC-DC Converter With Switched Capacitor Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a new topology of bidirectional hybrid DC-DC converters, where the main advantage is the inclusion of an inductor in series with a switched capacitors, which reduces the peak current values. Additionally, it is possible to use low capacitance values, as even with the capacitor operating in full charge mode, current peaks will be reduced. The theoretical evaluation presented in the paper focuses on analyzing the benefits for both operating modes, theoretical waveforms, and voltage stresses on the components. To validate the theoretical data, in addition to simulations, a $12 \mathrm{~V} / 48 \mathrm{~V}$ prototype was developed. Through this prototype, it was possible to confirm the theoretical studies developed regarding the proposed new bidirectional converter topology.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Controller for Grid-Forming Inverters applied to Single-Phase Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper features the use of a model reference adaptive controller (MRAC) for the inner loop of a grid-forming inverter (GFM). The gradient algorithm is based on the discrete-time model of the converter and its state variables feedback. An adaptive control law is particularly suitable for a GFM due to its high parameter uncertainties. During island operation, the load impedance could vary from open circuit to its nominal load, and when connected to the main grid, the impedance at the point of common coupling (PCC) is also unknown.

articleTitle: Optimal Phasor Measurement Unit Placement Using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) plays a massive role in dynamic monitoring and wide-area protection of the power system. Although installing PMU on each bus makes sense, it is unrealistic due to the high cost and unnecessary. Given these circumstances, academia and industry have been researching to find the best algorithm for Optimal Phasor Measurement Unit Placement (OPP). The OPP is primarily driven by economic and observability issues, among others. Traditionally, all OPP strategies frame OPP as an optimization problem and use various optimization algorithms to find the best solution. In this paper, a Machine Learning (ML) technique based on a data-driven approach is investigated. The proposed novel algorithm makes use of the Real-time Simulator (OPAL-RT) to extract data and the Random Forest Method to detect the physical anomaly in the power system. The results are further processed to find the best solution for PMU placement. The proposed approach is applied in the IEEE 9-bus system to validate its effectiveness. The regression technique is used to verify the ability of the approach to maximize the observability of the entire system.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Between Discrete-time Differentiators for Sensorless PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Efficiency and precision in controlling permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) are crucial for industrial and automotive applications, especially electric vehicle traction. This paper explores discrete-time differentiation techniques for estimating rotor speed and position in PMSMs, which is essential for effective operation. Traditional sensor-based methods, while accurate, are complex, costly, and prone to failure, leading to the development of sensorless techniques, primarily based on Back-Electromotive Force (BEMF) estimation. Differentiating the BEMF’s electrical angle is a common approach to observing rotor speed. This study compares first-order, central difference, state variable filter (SVF), super-twisting sliding mode (STSM), and phase-locked loop (PLL) differentiation methods. Through mathematical analysis and Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation, SVF and STSM are identified as providing superior noise mitigation and accurate estimates in transient and steady-state conditions.

articleTitle: A robust MPC for grid-following inverters improved with the krill herd optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: LCL filters are commonly used to interface the inverters and the electrical grid on grid-tied systems. However, its control is a challenge due to the resonance peak. Conversely, its model is well-known. Taking this into account, this work presents a model predictive controller with a robust adaptive disturbance rejection to control the grid-injected current of a voltage source inverter with an LCL filter. In addition, the disturbance rejection controller is tuned with the krill herd optimization algorithm. An in-depth discussion about optimizer configuration is provided to assist controller designers. The results demonstrated that system response has a short transient regime, around a quarter grid cycle, even when grid impedance changes.

articleTitle: An artificial bee colony optimizer-based FOC for PMSG-based wind energy conversion systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: The world is experiencing a transformation in the energy sector driven by the urgent need to address the escalating climate crisis, which is intensified due to the traditional power generation systems. In this context, wind energy conversion systems (WECS) emerge as a prominent solution for large-scale sustainable power generation. Particularly, direct drive permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSG) have garnered significant attention due to their structural advantages, which eliminates the drivetrain, leading to reduced maintenance costs. Field oriented control (FOC) is largely employed in the PMSG-based wind energy conversion systems. However, the tuning of the controllers to achieve the maximum power generation can be a laborious process. Addressing this challenge, this work presents a meta-heuristic-based controller parametrization grounded on the artificial bee colony optimization algorithm. The systematic method considers current tracking minimization and voltage constraints for synthetization of the control actions. The outcomes of 60 simulations corroborate the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed parametrization procedure. Furthermore, the WECS with the optimized FOC can extract almost 10 MW when the nominal wind speed reaches around $11 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.

articleTitle: State-of-Art Consumer Behavior in Response to Price Signals in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Microgrids emerged as a response to the need to reduce carbon emissions. These small-scale energy networks operate similarly to traditional utilities but stand out for their greater autonomy and focus on sustainable energy generation alternatives. In addition, microgrids can operate both connected to the conventional grid and in isolation, ensuring energy self-sufficiency. Given the importance of these systems, the objective is to map, quantify, and analyze existing publications on microgrids, focusing on user behavior in response to price signals and identifying research trends and main aspects studied in the literature. For this, a literature review with specific keywords in scientific databases (Scopus and Web of Science) was used, resulting in the analysis of 392 documents after removing duplicates. The analysis of the studies revealed a significant increase in publications on microgrids, highlighting the topic’s relevance. It was identified that user response to price signals is crucial for efficiently managing microgrids, emphasizing advanced technologies such as Internet of Things and smart meters.

articleTitle: Automatic Control of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Using a Novel Application Programming Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a machine-to-machine solution which aims on simultaneous and remote control of several electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs). It uses an application programming interface (API) integrated with General Public Licence 3.0 (GPL3) software and was designed as a tool to control EVCS’ power dispatch. The solution proposed in this paper is tailored for use with the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), thus being compatible with a wide range of EVCSs already available in the industry. Moreover, the control scheme presented in this paper facilitates the implementation of dynamic pricing and demand-response mechanisms, necessary to business models seeking to fully integrate e-mobility with distribution grid and renewable energy resources. To verify the efficacy of the proposed solution, software-based validation is used for the API along with EV charge operations. Finally, this paper concludes with the insights gleaned from validation analysis and its discussion.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of 2D/3D Flow of Natural Ester Through Power Transformer Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Given the critical role of power transformers in electrical power systems, continuous improvements in their thermal performance to extend their operational lifespan are essential. In this context, this study presents a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model to determine the detailed temperature distribution within the high-voltage (HV) winding of a step-up power transformer. The developed model analyzes the oil flow through the windings using natural ester, employing both a 3D model and an axisymmetric 2D domain. The results obtained from these simulations were compared with data available in the literature. The findings were satisfactory, demonstrating significant differences between the 3D and 2D domains in terms of the temperature profile along the HV winding disks and the oil hotspot temperature.

articleTitle: Swarm Intelligence-Based PID Tuning for Drone Control in Photovoltaic Panel Monitoring using Fire Hawk Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: José Eduardo Das Neves Da Fonseca
Paulo J. Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: The increasing demand for energy, driven by population growth and the expansion of industrialization, has led to the adoption of a more diversified and sustainable global energy matrix. In this sense, photovoltaic power generation systems have emerged as a versatile and popular renewable energy system. Solar panels, known for their high energy output and low cost, are widely used in both industrial and residential settings. However, maintaining these panels operating at nominal conditions requires regular inspections to identify potential issues such as scratches, erosion, and dust accumulation, which can significantly reduce energy efficiency of these devices. Traditional inspection methods are time-consuming and costly, especially for large installations. The use of drones equipped with cameras for efficient and safe photovoltaic panel inspections is currently gaining attention worldwide. However, a sophisticated control system is necessary to ensure precise and stable drone flight. While traditional PID controllers are commonly used for their simplicity and cost-effectiveness, tuning the PID parameters is challenging for highly dynamical systems such as drones, and they are often designed with suboptimal performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a nature-inspired meta-heuristic algorithm-based controller tuning methodology using the fire hawk optimization. The developed method has systematic rules to ensure that the drone achieves stable and precise flight when using the optimized drone controllers.

articleTitle: Dialogues On Renewable Energies: Impacts Of University
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The “Dialogues on Renewable Energies” extension project at the Federal University of Recôncavo da Bahia plays a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about renewable energies, adopting online and hybrid formats to democratize access to technical and scientific knowledge. This project was carried out in the 2021, 2022 and 2023 editions, always in the second half of the year, with a program made up of lectures, exhibitions, mini-courses, technical visits, round tables and debates on renewable energy issues, totaling 29 activities/events spread over the three years of the project, which had a registered audience of 1503 people. Thus, each activity invited specialists, scientists and professionals working in the energy market in order to contribute to the academic training of UFRB students as well as informing/stimulating the relevance of the topic to the entire external community at local and national level. With more than 3,000 unique views on its YouTube channel and initiatives such as the “Minicurso de Eléctrica Predial” to train women, the project promotes inclusion and gender equality in the sector. In addition, by ensuring accessibility for people with hearing and/or visual impairments, the project demonstrates a real commitment to inclusion. The comprehensive evaluations at the end of each edition revealed a significant uptake by the community, both academic and external, highlighting the growing interest in the topic of renewable energies and the positive impact on promoting critical thinking and research. The effective integration of the pillars of research, extension and teaching demonstrates the importance of the university as a transforming agent in the dissemination of scientific knowledge and in fostering interest in research, both inside and outside the academic environment.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis through Merit Indexes of a Carport located in Neoville campus of the Federal University of Technology of Paraná
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Indeed, the primary source of GHG (greenhouse gas) emissions is the transport sector. Thus, an alternative to decarbonization is adopting together EVs and Renewable energy sources. By the way, a Solar Carport can obey these conditions since it integrates an EV charge station and a grid-connected PV system. Consequently, this current article presents a comparative analysis through merit indexes cited in the IEC61724 between a Solar Carport and a grid-connected PV system called EPESOL, both located in the Neoville campus of the Federal University of Technology of Paraná (UTFPR).

articleTitle: Co-design of Plant and Controller Parameters for Grid-Tied Inverters: Metaheuristics based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: One subject that can be more explored in control applied to power electronics is the simultaneous design of the converter and control parameters, in order to improve robustness and performance. For instance, if the filter parameters of a power converter were designed together with the control gains, one could seek, simultaneously, optimized indices for both the filter and the controller. In this context, this paper proposes the simultaneous design of LCL filter parameters and current control gains for grid-tied inverters. The cost function is written as a weighted sum of the inductances and capacitance of the filter and a mean squared error for grid currents in a typical test of sinusoidal reference tracking. The cost function also incorporates important constraints for both filter and controller designs as penalty factors. A particle swarm optimization is then used to find, simultaneously, the parameters of the LCL filter and of a state feedback controller, which brings advantages over a conventional sequential design, as shown by examples. Results in control hardware-in-the-loop attest the efficacy of the proposal.

articleTitle: An enhanced RMRAC-based PI controller for grid-tied voltage source inverters with LLCL filters using the dragonfly optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: Renewable energy systems have expanded considerably in the last decade due to their technological advances that make them economically competitive. In these systems, high-order filters are employed to reduce inverter harmonics. However, these filters pose a challenge to system stability due to their inherent resonances. This work proposes a hybrid controller for grid-tied systems with LLCL filters, composed of a proportional-integral controller and robust model reference adaptive controller. Furthermore, the control system gains are tuned with a systematic procedure based on the dragonfly optimization algorithm, considering tracking error minimization and control action synthetization constraints. The results indicate high robustness and fast response of the optimized controller with developed parametrization procedure.

articleTitle: Analysis of Renewable-Based Microgrid Energy Management and the Impact of Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Rising global energy demand has depleted conventional resources and increased greenhouse gas emissions. To counter this, renewable energy adoption is growing. Microgrids (MG), which combine conventional generators, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and distributed energy resources (DER) offer a solution by enhancing efficiency and reliability. This paper presents an analysis of energy management within a MG with and without energy storage. The MG includes solar, wind and biogas generators, accounting the power losses. A rule-based method was employed to manage the power flow, ensuring reliable operation. The BESS increased the MG ‘s flexibility by charging and discharging according to the most advantageous scenarios for the microgrid, and reduced the overall operational costs compared to the MG without storage. The paper analyzed the impact of BESS in a MG and the proposed approach ensured power balance and maximized the utilization of the available DER.

articleTitle: Analysis of Feature Selection in Self Organizing Map Model Performance for Energy Theft Areas Identification.
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents a case study on electricity theft in an area of the city of Florianópolis, in the state of Santa Catarina (SC), Brazil. The main objective is to identify areas (clusters) using feature selection and self-organizing maps (SOM). A decision tree algorithm is used to select socioeconomic variables that best explain the density of fraud cases occurring in the study area. That is, a consumer unit associated with a case of theft has their geographic coordinates, as well as socioeconomic parameters according to its location, thus, with feature selection the parameters that best relates to the case of fraud are selected as entry for the SOM model. Two sets of variables (raw and selection) are used as entries for the SOM model, it is observed that the model with the selection of variables had better performance in assigning weights to areas with a greater probability of energy theft occurring, since that dimensionality reduction helps in better differentiation in weight assignments by the algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancing quarter car active suspension performance using walrus optimization algorithm-based PID controller
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: The suspension system of a vehicle is one of the main components of security and comfort for the driver and the car passengers. Therefore, the use of precise controller is vital to ensure the reliability of these vehicles. This paper presents a novel approach to tuning the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller of an active suspension system using the walrus optimization algorithm (WOA). This bioinspired meta-heuristic technique is used to find the optimal gains for the PID controller considering the minimization of the mean absolute tracking error. Systematic rules are defined to drive the optimization procedure of the controller. The system is simulated in three scenarios: a flat road, a speed bump, and a pothole, allowing to evaluate the adaptability of the controller in average traffic conditions. The results of 50 experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in finding the best gains for the controller, resulting in satisfactory performance and minimizing the tracking error to a residual value. A comparison with the classical closed-loop Ziegler & Nichols method is provided, where the proposed method ensures a tracking error reduction of ${9 4. 7 6 \%}$ and a root mean square error reduction of ${9 4. 3 3 \%}$. Additionally, the overshoot during the startup transient regime was reduced by ${9 0. 6 6 \%}$, while also eliminating the settling time of the system when evaluated utilizing the $2 \%$ criteria.

articleTitle: Optimal vector control of a DFIG-based wind energy conversion energy system using bald eagle search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: The climate crisis is a reality that has impacted billions of people around the world. The fast-growing industrialization demands energy at an ever-increasing rate. However, traditional power generation systems are significantly responsible for the current environmental crisis. One way to mitigate the energy sector’s impact and contribute to environmental balance is to increase power generation from renewable sources. Wind energy is promising, but it requires sophisticated controllers to ensure efficiency. This work presents the optimization of vector control for a wind energy conversion system based on a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG). The optimization utilizes the bald eagle search (BES) algorithm, a modern meta-heuristic optimization algorithm. The results demonstrated that the gains obtained through BES effectively control the rotor voltages and currents, ensuring system stability and maximizing power generation. Therefore, the meta-heuristic-based control design method offers a systematic procedure for designing vector control, effectively automating this task.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of a Control System for Yaw Damper
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Ensuring the stability and control of aircraft is essential in aerospace engineering, especially for large commercial aircraft such as the Boeing 747. Stability during flight is difficult to maintain due to the aircraft’s substantial size and speed, necessitating the minimization of yaw oscillations for passenger comfort and safety reasons. This study aims to create a robust and adaptive yaw damping control system that combines various control strategies for large aircraft. The approach involves designing a controller based on the aircraft state-space model, utilizing stability derivatives, and conducting closed-loop simulations. The developed control system demonstrates enhanced yaw stability, with simulations showing a rapid return to equilibrium and significant oscillation damping. By employing an integrated methodology, this research advances the development of safer and more efficient systems for large commercial aircraft.

articleTitle: Comparative Analyzes of Parameters Extraction Models for Photovoltaic Modules Using Single Diode Model
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Modeling photovoltaic modules using electrical circuit models is crucial for accurately predicting power generation in PV systems. The primary challenge involves determining the electrical parameters of these models to accurately forecast PV behavior under varying weather conditions throughout the system’s operation. This study compares the Villalva, De Soto, California Energy Commission, and Sandia Single Diode Models—the latter having been utilized by PVSYST since version 6—for establishing the initial electrical parameters, according to the method. The parameters determined by the first three models are recalculated for different values of irradiance and temperature using the De Soto physical model. To validate the models’ simulations, real-world energy generation data from a PV system from the west of São Paulo state, for the year 2020 was analyzed. This data includes solar irradiance in the plane of array (POA) and PV module temperatures, monitored by local sensors.

articleTitle: Enhancing solar photovoltaic systems: a soft-computing optimization of the solar tracker actuator using horned lizard algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: Solar photovoltaic systems can be equipped with solar tracker actuators to follow up the maximum solar irradiance on the panel, aiming to provide maximum power generation. This kind of actuator is generally a DC motor, which moves the panel when necessary in accordance with sun movement. This work presents a soft-computing controller tuning method for a solar tracker actuator. The developed method uses the horned lizard algorithm with a set of systematic rules to provide an optimized proportional-integral controller that regulates the system regulator. The results indicate that this modern approach enhances the system’s performance, making it track the reference quickly. A comparison with Ziegler-Nichols indicate the superiority of the proposed tuning method.

articleTitle: Energy measurement based on self-calibration and non-self-calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this article, we present a mathematical simulation designed to calculate the errors associated with a public lighting measurement system. The system measures current through a shunt resistor and voltage using a resistive divider. Additionally, it calculates active power and total harmonic distortion (THD). To quantify uncertainties, the simulation considers factors such as offset and gain errors, temperature effects, and component parameter variations. Finally, we compare the results of the simulation with and without calibration, demonstrating a significant improvement in accuracy when calibration is applied.

articleTitle: An LQR with adaptive disturbance rejection for grid-tied systems tuned with the cuckoo optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: Grid-tied inverters are commonly used in renewable energy conversion systems. These inverters generate harmonics due to the switching dynamics. Thus, LCL filters are used in the inverter output. However, a resonance peak is induced due to the filter dynamics, which can lead the system to instability. In light of this concern, this work proposes a new hybrid controller composed of a linear quadratic regulator for grid-injected current control along with a robust model reference adaptive controller for disturbance rejection on a grid-tied system with LCL filter. In addition, a parametrization procedure based on the cuckoo search optimization algorithm is provided. Simulation results of 35 experiments indicate that the developed controller has high performance and robustness.

articleTitle: Enhanced PI controllers for wind turbines with direct drive permanent magnet synchronous generators using bat optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias De Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: The world claims for immediate power generation transition towards a fully clean and sustainable energy matrix. In this sense, wind energy plays a crucial role in the success of this new power generation era. Permanent magnet synchronous generators are at the core of the wind energy conversion systems. These devices are subjected to a well-designed control mechanism to ensure stability and efficiency during the overall energy conversion process. The optimal torque control for maximum power point tracking associated with the field oriented controller is largely utilized in these systems. However, the performance of proportional-integral controllers employed on generators is highly dependable on controller design expertise. Therefore, this work presents a systematic controller design based on the bat optimization algorithm, which provides stability and fast response for dq current tracking, considering variable wind speeds.

articleTitle: An ant lion optimizer-based PI controller with robust ADRC for LLCL filter current regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald
José E. Das Neves Da Fonseca

abstract: The climate crisis is marked by the deterioration of the climate due to increased greenhouse gas emissions, resulting in extreme weather events and threatening the environmental and social stability of the planet. Renewable energy conversion systems have emerged as potential solutions to combat this global problem. In this context, grid-tied power systems with high-order filters are essential for implementing the energy matrix transition. This work presents a simple and effective grid-injected current controller with adaptive disturbance rejection controller for grid-tied inverters with LLCL filters along with a controller parametrization procedure based on ant lion optimizer. The results indicate the feasibility of the proposed control systems ensuring fast and precise current tracking, satisfactory disturbance rejection, and robustness to grid impedance variations.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization Framework for University’s Residential Halls: Striving for Sustainable Institutions
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper outlines an energy management drive carried out at halls of residence of the University of Engineering and Technology Lahore (RCET Campus).Goals of the drive were to discover; pattern of energy consumption by students, figuring out reasons of energy wastage and suggesting energy-saving measures for the hostels. An interview survey was conducted to learn about the demographics and perspectives of the students. The research suggests installing prepaid meters, changing inefficient CFLs and tube lights with LED lights, and replacing inefficient old fans with energy efficient fans to cut energy use. The findings of this study provide promising possibilities for educational institutional hostels to significantly cut their energy consumption. The study offers the possibility of saving 58.2%, 37% and 50% energy in lighting load, fan load, and through geysers automation, respectively. All of these efforts result in an overall energy savings of 49% and a consequent reduction of USD 12827 in electricity bills. Hence it would be beneficial to university economically.

articleTitle: Temporal Causality Analysis and Energy Efficiency: Impact of the Compressed Air System on Electrical Energy Consumption in an Automotive Metalworking Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate the causality effects on the variation of electrical energy consumption and the energy efficiency of the compressed air system of an automotive metalworking industry in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. Two industrial plants were studied, with measurements taken over seven days, revealing that approximately 20% of the company’s total electrical energy consumption is due to the compressed air generation system. Using the Granger Causality technique, the relationship between air flow and power used is proven. The test resulted in the rejection of the null hypothesis that flow causes power, indicating that the demand for compressed air has a direct and proportional impact on electrical energy consumption, despite the different influences of the system’s fixed and variable compressors. An alarming fact is the high grid demand even without production, indicating significant waste of air and energy. This scenario highlights the need for optimizations, such as minimizing leaks and replacing the extensive use of compressed air with more efficient and economical methods for cooling machines and equipment.

articleTitle: A soft-computing parametrization procedure for DFIG-based wind turbines using Seagull optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: Traditional energy generation methods are one of the major contributors to the current climate crisis. Transitioning to renewable energy sources, such as wind power, is essential for restoring ecological equilibrium. However, optimizing the efficiency of wind energy systems necessitates sophisticated control mechanisms. This study presents the optimization of the controllers of a wind energy conversion system (WECS) based on a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) using the modern soft-computing technique known as seagull optimization algorithm (SOA). Systematic rules are proposed to drive the optimization procedure using SOA that effectively tunes the DFIG-based WECS control system, ensuring efficient regulation of rotor and stator dynamics to maximize power generation. The results corroborate the feasibility and high performance of the developed methodology for controller tuning.

articleTitle: Control Optimization of a 2 MW DFIG-based Wind Turbine using Sparrow Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: This work presents a methodology for tuning the PI controllers of a 2 MW double-fed induction generator-based wind energy conversion system. The results indicate that the developed methodology, utilizing systematic rules, can provide sets of gains that ensure satisfactory system response. Results from 50 experiments demonstrate the efficiency and stability of the PI controllers optimized by our methodology. Additionally, all obtained solutions are implementable, as they require less voltage to be synthesized than the available DC voltage link. Furthermore, the optimized controller ensures that the generator currents approach their reference values quickly, generating around 2 MW in the nominal wind speed condition.
