Thus, the developed meta-heuristic-based methodology serves as a valuable tool for control designers, helping to maximize the power generation from wind energy.

articleTitle: Dynamic Pricing-Driven Framework for Optimizing Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents a framework for calculating the hourly electricity price, considering the relationship between energy consumption and energy price in such a way to achieve the consumption closer to a given target. This framework considers a general definition between energy consumption and price, the objective function as a distance metric from the desired target, and a set of constraints. Two optimization methods were tested, the Trust-Region Constrained method and Sequential-Least Squares Programming (SLSQP). The results showed that it is possible to model the consumption/price relationship dynamically, and that this scenario was designed to encourage consumption outside of peak hours, not being restricted to the two forms of modeling presented. This aspect is particularly useful for short and long-term financial planning for energy suppliers. This flexibility in pricing strategies is a significant advancement in understanding consumer behavior in response to price changes. The paper opens avenues for further exploration, such as investigating alternative linear constraints, different price limits, and varying time intervals for consumption. This suggests a pathway for enhancing the framework’s applicability and effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimizing PID Controllers of Drone-based Wind Turbine Inspection Systems using the African Vulture Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: José Eduardo Das Neves Da Fonseca
Paulo J. Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: The inspection and maintenance of wind turbines are critical tasks, often challenged by their height and the extensive area they cover. The use of drones, or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), has emerged as an efficient solution, offering agility, safety, and reliability. These vehicles can be equipped with onboard image processing systems and sensors, allowing them to detect weathering effects such as cracks, burns, and erosion on turbine blades. However, achieving the precision required for effective monitoring necessitates a stable vehicle with a precise path-following. In this sense, the design of the flight controllers is fundamental to ensure quality in the measurements and images acquired by the inspection system installed in the drone. The most common control strategy adopted to regulate drone dynamics is the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. However, determining its optimal gains is complex due to the dynamic nature of drone flight. This paper explores the use of the African Vulture algorithm, a nature-inspired meta-heuristic optimizer, to tune the PID controller gains efficiently. The developed method aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of drone-based wind turbine inspections, reducing material damage and ensuring precise sensor readings. The results indicate that the optimized PID controller for the UAV-based inspection system ensures high performance for path tracking, being a feasible tool to optimize this flight control system.

articleTitle: High-performance quarter car active suspension system using PID controller tuned by the dingo optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson Dias de Oliveira Evald

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for tuning a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller applied to the active suspension system of an electric vehicle using the dingo optimization algorithm (DOA). The DOA is utilized as the core of a sophisticated controller tuning method and follows systematic rules to provide optimal gains to the PID, enhancing vehicle stability. As an outcome, the security and the comfort of the driver and passengers are increased, once the optimized controller can minimize the vehicle balance on irregular land. The active suspension model is based on a quarter-car representation. Three scenarios were considered in the simulation, including a flat road, a speed bump, and a road with a hole. The results demonstrate that the DOA-tuned PID controller effectively minimizes tracking errors, ensuring stable and precise control of the suspension system without excessive control effort. Another meta-heuristic approach was used for comparison, the Whale optimizer algorithm (WOA). The proposed controller presented superior performance, not developing the oscillatory behavior of the WOA-tuned algorithm. Moreover, the settling time using the proposed control approach is null. In this sense, the developed control system enhances the comfort and security of the driver and passengers.

articleTitle: Implementation Positive Feedback of Voltage and Frequency for Islanding Detection of Distributed Generations
publicationTitle: 2024 16th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In energy generation, environmental and energy crises include the extensive application of renewable energy, such as wind energy and photovoltaic energy. These energy generations are highly dependent on power electronic converters to transform the electricity generated and connect it to the grid, in the form of distributed generation (DG). The event in which the DG remains connected to the point of common coupling (PCC) when there is a drop in grid voltage is known as islanding. In national and international standards, disconnection of the DG from the PCC is required. For this purpose, relays that monitor electrical parameters already establish protection for connection only in nominal operation. However, in some critical situations, these relays are not capable of detecting islanding. Thus, the present study is dedicated to the implementation in Matlab/Simulink of a DG model with a three-phase current controller converter, and anti-islanding positive feedback (feedback AI) which causes destabilization necessary to assist the protective relays. It was observed that the DG model follows the requirements of international standards regarding synchronism stability. It was also observed that in the critical situation for the protective relays, the active methods were effective in quickly destabilizing the island, causing irrelevant effects on the level of total harmonic distortion (THD).
